promises.quote: We have further emphasised the importance of the Missing Persons (MISPER) process to all our staff on these units, including making this a part of our improvement work in the reduction of the numbers of people who may be Absence Without Leave (AWOL). A member of the Clinical Assurance team is specifically assigned to wards with the view to ensure compliance with the MISPER agreement is tested.
promises.summary: Assign Clinical Assurance staff to monitor MISPER compliance on wards

reports.title: Melanie Elms: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: The care package arranged for Melanie following discharge from lengthy in-patient admission was not followed and was altered to something which the treating doctor did not consider adequate
The walk book was not properly completed

There was no extra planning for changes in circumstances: Melanie faced never being allowed to return to family life with her husband and son due to Child In Need proceedings; changes in medication and less support from family due to the Social Services requirements
concerns.hazard: lack of extra planning for changes in circumstances

concerns.quote: There was no missing person plan in place with timeframe and steps of escalation for Melanie's leave
Risk assessment prior to leave was not adequate
concerns.hazard: inadequate risk assessment prior to leave

concerns.quote: Risk assessment prior to leave was not recorded

categories: Alcohol, drug and medication related deaths
Community health care and emergency services related deaths

concerns.quote: The court heard evidence that Mr Savory did not return at the agreed time of 18:35 on 26 January 2020 and that staff were aware that he had not returned from 18:45 onwards

links.explanation: Both reports highlight a lack of clear timing for initiating missing‑person procedures when patients do not return as expected. The earlier report focuses on absent written policy/timeframe for detained patients, while the later report points to staff unawareness of the immediate reporting requirement for informal patients.
links.earlier_quote: The timeframe for reporting informal patients to the police as missing persons if they fail to return at the agreed time.
links.later_quote: staff were aware that he had not returned from 18:45 onwards. The court found that thereafter there was a delay of approximately two hours in instituting the missing persons protocol
links.promise_quote: This issue is going to be covered in the new policy regarding leave for informal patients, as outlined above. We are also going to update our Section 17 Leave policy (for detained patients) and our Absent Without Leave policy with the same guidance.

links.explanation: Both reports highlight the absence of a clear timeframe and procedure for reporting patients who go missing during leave.
links.earlier_quote: - The timeframe for reporting informal patients to the police as missing persons if they fail to return at the agreed time.
links.later_quote: There was no missing person plan in place with timeframe and steps of escalation for Melanie's leave.
links.promise_quote: This issue is going to be covered in the new policy regarding leave for informal patients, as outlined above. We are also going to update our Section 17 Leave policy (for detained patients) and our Absent Without Leave policy with the same guidance.

links.explanation: Both reports highlight failures in timely activation of missing‑person protocols due to insufficient staff training/awareness.
links.earlier_quote: - Training procedures in respect of the police and hospital staff on Elgar Ward in the case of reports of missing persons and lack of understanding of areas of responsibility and appropriate actions.
links.later_quote: The court heard evidence from some members of staff who gave evidence that they were not aware of a particular timeframe for instigating the missing persons protocol in relation to informal patients, and as such I consider there is a risk of future delays in reporting informal patients as missing persons to police, which presents a risk of future deaths.
